ohne_zeug.satz: Your AI forgets you after every chat.
Desktop app · no cloud · no account · encrypted at rest SQLite · hybrid retrieval · knowledge graph · MCP
The machine state printed in the same artefacts says why no millisecond there is claimed as a verdict.
What a frame costs at each size is timed in [docs/graph-kosten.md](docs/graph-kosten.md), not claimed in this caption — a millisecond number is only worth the quiet machine that produced it.
The third view, *Semantic*, places the same notes by what their texts mean — no screenshot of it here yet.
Every memory carries a validity window, so the graph can be replayed: pull the time slider back, and every note that was not true yet at that moment dims — not deleted, simply not true *yet*.
The same question works in search (asOf in the HTTP API and MCP) and in the editor, where every note shows its *valid from / valid until*.
The next day you open a fresh chat and it knows none of it.
Agent | An AI program that can use tools instead of only answering — Claude Desktop, Cursor or Gemini CLI, for instance.
K3PTA stores the database key there, so there is no password to type.
No upload, no account, no telemetry.
One brain for every AI tool.
On a four-note check (npm run embed:sprachtest) the default model answers 4 of 4 English paraphrase questions and 1 of 4 of the same questions translated into German.
Changing the default would also mean re-embedding every stored note, because each chunk is keyed to the model that produced it (npm run eval:sprache reruns both sides).
Everything lives in ~/.kepta/, encrypted on disk, no account, no telemetry.
Files imported with an older extraction can be read again under *Settings → Data → Re-read imported files* — it counts first and writes only after you confirm

Import your AI history: bring your ChatGPT or Claude data export here (*Settings → Data management → Import your AI history*): every conversation with at least one answer becomes a searchable note with its original date,
Persistent embeddings via Ollama (nomic-embed-text), computed by a background queue instead of re-embedding on every query

Settings live in the encrypted data directory, not in browser storage — the desktop shell binds to a free port that changes on every launch, and localStorage is keyed by origin, so anything kept there was gone after a re
Read straight from the local database: no AI involved, nothing leaves the computer

Careful on purpose: only facts and how-tos are compared, both sentences must share their meaningful words, notes from the same file stay out, and so do the parts of a split file (README — 5/17), a note's source line and
No license server, no phone-home, no extra infrastructure — one file.
Model discovery for Ollama and LM Studio in one click, no key required
Duplicate review — every group side by side, one click to keep the richest copy or dismiss the pair for good.
Text size — 100, 115 or 130 %, under *Settings → Display*.
- All data in ~/.kepta/ — one SQLite file that belongs to you
- No account, no telemetry, no phone-home — and nothing to activate: the app validates no key, so there is no check of any kind to call home for.
- With no AI configured, not a single byte leaves the machine
No service in between, no account, no telemetry.
Your memories are stored only in that encrypted SQLite file — there is no server of mine for them to reach.
Standard library only, no dependencies.
There are two things in the world: K3PTA Core, free — the desktop app and the engine underneath it — and K3PTA Enterprise, memory for organizations, which exists only by agreement with Damian.
K3PTA's promise is a memory that is yours without supervision, so the whole mechanism was removed rather than tuned: no route, no header, no anchor, no strings.
Without that file there is no team workspace — the app says so plainly instead of hiding a dead end.
No plugin store, and that is not a lock.

K3PTA loads no third-party code, so there is nothing to approve, nothing to buy and nothing an organisation could switch off for you: the app's own features run the same in the free download as in a managed deployment.
There is no self-serve checkout anywhere, and there is no longer a key to issue for the app.

The engine underneath this app is source-available — BUSL-1.1, at [DamianTodorovic/kepta](https://github.com/DamianTodorovic/kepta) (each release converts to AGPL-3.0-or-later after four years): storage with encryption a

The packages are self-contained; you only need Node ≥ 22.13 to build them yourself.
